articles.title: The Dr. A. B. Gregory Award
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced Paul Mancuso as the recipient of the 2016 Dr. A. B. Gregory Award, recognizing his outstanding contributions to amateur astronomy. Mancuso was honored for his extensive service, including multiple terms on the SJAA Board and as Vice President, and his consistent participation in public outreach programs like School Star Parties and Solar Days. The article also provides a historical overview of the award, named after Dr. Boris Gregory, an influential former SJAA president known for his dedication to welcoming and assisting new astronomers.

articles.title: Member Recognition 2017
articles.summary: The article details the San José Astronomical Association's (SJAA) annual February membership meeting, where three long-serving members—Lee Hoglan, Ed Wong, and Dave Ittner—received recognition awards. These individuals were honored for their extensive contributions, leadership roles, and instrumental efforts in developing and managing numerous club programs such as the Telescope Loaner Program, Fix It sessions, Binocular Observing Program, and the QuickSTARt program, significantly advancing the club's mission and public outreach.

articles.title: SJAA Solar Party at Berryessa Branch Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) hosted a successful "Solar Party" at the Berryessa Branch Library on April 1, 2017. The event included a presentation by Bill & Susan O'Neil on "Our Magnetic Sun" and the upcoming 2017 Total Solar Eclipse, followed by safe solar observing with 10 telescopes for over 170 visitors to view sunspots, flares, and prominences.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation & Trip Reports
articles.summary: This SJAA compilation features multiple member observation reports, detailing various celestial sightings. Members describe viewing a very thin crescent moon and crescent Venus in late February 2017, along with an Aldebaran occultation by the moon's dark side in early March. The document also includes an email exchange about an astrophotography project utilizing the historic Lick Great Refractor and a report from a stargazing trip to Panamint Valley, emphasizing dark sky conditions and diverse observations.

articles.title: The Orbits of Jupiter's Moons Are Tilted
articles.summary: An amateur astronomer describes observing Jupiter's Galilean moons and noticing a significant change in their alignment between 2015 and 2016-2017. This shift, attributed to the tilt of the moons' orbits, meant that mutual events were absent in 2016-2017, and moons like Callisto appeared to pass above or below Jupiter rather than transiting it, leading to unique viewing patterns.

articles.title: SJAA School Program Post and a bit of History
articles.summary: The article presents a dual focus: first, a personal astronomy observing report from Panamint Valley, detailing successful deep-sky observations of numerous galaxies and the Milky Way, and a lunar occultation of Aldebaran. Second, it provides a statistical update on the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) 2016-2017 school program, outlining the number of completed, partially successful, and cancelled events based on sky conditions and planning status.

articles.title: History of the SJAA
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) began in December 1954, following an inquiry by William Weller in the San Jose Evening News. Initially called 'San Jose Amateur Astronomers,' the club officially incorporated in August 1955 and changed its name to SJAA in October 1978 to avoid negative connotations of the word 'amateur.' The article also touches upon the evolution of their meeting locations and the naming of their newsletter, 'Ephemeris.'

articles.title: Total Solar Eclipse
articles.summary: This article details the Total Solar Eclipse occurring on Monday, August 21, 2017, which will be visible across North America. It explains that observers within a thin path of totality stretching from Oregon to South Carolina will witness the moon completely cover the sun, revealing the corona, while those outside this path will experience a partial eclipse. The longest duration of totality will be approximately two minutes and 40 seconds, with the event covering portions of 14 U.S. states.

articles.title: Ocean Worlds Are All Around Us
articles.summary: Recent findings from NASA's Cassini mission and Hubble Space Telescope highlight the potential habitability of icy moons in our solar system. Cassini discovered hydrogen gas, a chemical energy source for life, resulting from hydrothermal activity on Saturn's moon Enceladus. Simultaneously, Hubble provided additional evidence of erupting plumes on Jupiter's moon Europa, intensifying the scientific interest in these "ocean worlds" and the search for extraterrestrial life.

articles.title: Crab Nebula
articles.summary: Astronomers have created a highly detailed, multi-wavelength composite image of the Crab Nebula, combining data from five telescopes across the electromagnetic spectrum (radio to X-ray). The article explains that the Crab Nebula is a supernova remnant from an explosion observed in 1054, located 6,500 light-years from Earth, and features a rapidly rotating neutron star (pulsar) at its core that shapes the nebula. This combined view reveals the complex interplay of the pulsar, its particle wind, and the supernova's ejected material.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article showcases an astrophotography gallery featuring images captured by SJAA members Swaroop Shere and guest speaker Seth Eddy. The gallery highlights stunning photos of deep-sky objects like the Dumbbell Nebula (M27), the Leo Triplet, and M51, complete with detailed technical specifications of the imaging equipment, software, and capture settings used for each submission.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This article features a "Kid Spot" section with space-themed jokes and a quiz on fundamental astronomy concepts, including answers. Additionally, it presents a historical overview titled "100 Years of Astronomical Discovery," detailing significant milestones from 1913 to 1919, such as the invention of the Ritchey-Chretien telescope, the discovery of white dwarfs and Proxima Centauri, and early work on black holes and large observatories. The content appears to be from the June 2017 edition of SJAA EPHEMERIS.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board of Directors met in February, March, and April 2017, discussing a range of club operations. Key topics included improvements to the membership database and website, procurement of new equipment for the solar program and speaker system, and officer elections. The board also addressed public outreach initiatives, event planning, and guidelines for astrophotography at observing sites.

articles.title: SJAA Library & Programs
articles.summary: The SJAA offers a variety of resources and programs for its members and the community, including a library of astronomy books and DVDs. They provide practical services such as free telescope repair and a loaner equipment program. Additionally, the association hosts regular observing events like solar and night sky sessions, alongside educational initiatives such as the Quick STARt program for beginners and specialized astrophotography workshops and interest groups.
